title: II.11: Fugue in F major

groocock.chapter: 7 Group 2: Fugues for Three Voices, without Stretto

entries.notes: tonal; tonic retained until second half of bar 7; accompanied by leaping fifths/fourths figure
enters as if on third beat of a 6/8 bar because of the canon cross-rhythm
redundant entry; uses B-natural so it is entirely in the dominant (OCR "Bk")
only entry outside the keys of the exposition
suggests answer at its beginning; extended by sequence to six bars; new demisemiquaver accompaniment

episodes.material: second figure of bar 3 and first figure of bar 4 linked by tied note; two-part canon at the fourth below after one bar (or sixth above after one beat); soprano alone in 3/4 cross-rhythm
bar 4 in three-part imitation with jerky rhythm of bars 6-7

episodes.to_key: I (transient modulations to vi, ii, v)
episodes.material: four sections: 25-29 rising sequence in bass with ep.2 material; 29-37 develops ep.2 (V to vi and ii); 37-45 canon of ep.1 in duple time; 45-52 return to 25-29 material with transient modulations
56-61 development of ep.1, new canon at the sixth above at one beat; 61-66 decorated suspensions above a dominant pedal in IV
70-76 new canon (soprano leads, middle a seventh below) IV-bVII-dominant of I; 76-85 recalls 61-65 over dominant pedal in I minor

countersubjects.notes: no regular countersubject; accompaniment different each time; recurring figures mainly rhythmic; only recognizable melodic line soprano 16-18 used again 23-25

subject.notes: subject begins with tonic ornamented by lower auxiliary (semitone); answer begins with dominant ornamented by a tone; fourth note dominant answered by tonic; p.6: semitone f-e-f answered by whole tone c-bb-c (diatonic auxiliary principle in reverse); II.21 treated similarly

key_plan: Group 2 table: Exp I V EP I | EP V | Dev EP I EP IV | Final EP I I

claims.claim: Exposition has an episode (bars 9-14) before the third entry; redundant answer at bar 21.
Only fugue in Group 2 with no entry in the relative minor/major; only one entry (IV) outside exposition keys.
Introducing fresh material (demisemiquavers) in the last bars is unlike Bach's usual practice; foreshadowed by run in bar 45.
No countersubject, but the exposition provides melodic or rhythmic figures for later development (with II.12, II.19).
